title: Why patients return to hospital from hospital at home
subtitle: Design not yet settled: the request asks why, not how often
statement: Patients treated in the hospital-at-home program appear to be readmitted more often than ward patients (17 against 12 percent at 30 days on the program dashboard), most visibly those with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart failure. The program does not know why patients return, whether returns follow clinical worsening, falls, carer strain or night-time gaps, or which returns could be avoided. Managers want the answer before adding beds.
whoAffected: Patients admitted to hospital at home (412 in the last year), their family carers, the program's nurses and physicians, and the managers deciding on expansion.
whatHurts: A readmission undoes the purpose of care at home, exposes frail patients to a hospital stay they hoped to avoid and can leave carers feeling they failed.
currentPractice: Readmissions are counted on a dashboard; their reasons and the patient and carer experience before the return are not recorded.
whyNow: An expansion decision next year and a dashboard figure that worries managers.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients who choose hospital at home stay at home safely when they can, and return to hospital only when hospital care is what they need.
summary: Problem framed around the unexplained readmissions; the design is left unresolved because the request does not say whether the aim is to measure, compare or explain.
